description:
Wibou's run: the clip he plays while moving on the ground. He is one of the fastest runners in the roster.

Who he is. Wibou is an ironic mall-ninja weeaboo: a cringe Neo from The Matrix with a katana, a black fedora, a dark open coat, black trousers and white sneakers (images 1-2, the real character in the game). He takes himself completely seriously, which is the joke, so play every pose sincerely, never winking. In the fight he is a quick, light spacing duelist who wins at the edge of his blade's reach and then chases opponents into the air. He holds the katana in his right hand; its home on the ground is low by his right hip, the blade pointing out to his right and back, nearly level, the tip about 1.5 m out to the right and 1 m behind the hips.

How the game plays it. The run loops: ticks 0-32 are 0.53 s and two steps, wrapping from 32 back to 0. He does not move in the clip; the game carries him at up to 10.6 m/s, so the feet cycle under the body as on a treadmill. The game plays the clip at his speed divided by 10.6, never below 0.35: a walk plays it at 0.4x, the first steps at 0.6x. Every pose must still read in slow motion. The game crossfades into the run from the idle (0.1 s) and out of it into the idle, the jump (0.05 s) and attacks. The match camera sits straight behind him.

The run, the ninja run, played completely straight:
- Legs, today's timing. The left foot strikes at tick 0 and the right at tick 16. Each foot lands under or a little ahead of the hips, on the ball of the foot, stays planted 6-7 ticks while it travels about 1.1-1.3 m back under the body, then the heel lifts, the toes bend as it pushes off, the knee comes up fast in front and the foot swings forward. A short flight between steps. Light and quick, not heavy.
- The floor: on today's idle a flat foot puts the toe joint at about up = -0.98 m in this character frame. Never push a foot through it.
- Body: the chest pitches well forward (head 0.3-0.5 m ahead of the hips), the head comes up so he looks ahead, the hat tilts with the lean.
- Arms: both swept straight back behind him, the anime ninja run. The left arm long behind, the hand open and relaxed. The sword arm back too, the katana trailing behind him and out to the right at a diagonal, so the camera behind him sees the blade's length, never end-on, and the tip stays clear of the legs.
- The arms must not lock. The shoulder blades and elbows bob with each step, the left hand flutters a little, and the blade bobs and settles 2-3 ticks after the body.
- Pelvis: it turns 6-10 degrees toward the forward leg on every step and shifts 2-4 cm over the stance foot; the hips drop 6-10 cm into each landing and rise in the push-off. The chest counter-turns a little, less than in an arm-swinging run because the arms stay back. The head bobs less than the hips and 2-3 ticks later.
- The coat is spring-driven in the game: the hips' bob and turn are what make it flap.

No props other than the katana, no spins, no attack.

Secondary motion, with numbers:
- Coat: the hips bob 6-10 cm, turn 6-10 degrees each way and shift 2-4 cm over the stance foot; that drives the coat's flap.
- Hat: the head bobs 40-70% of the hips' bob, 2-3 ticks after them, and pitches 2-4 degrees with each landing, so the fedora nods with the step but never bounces.
- Sword: the tip bobs 4-15 cm and lags the hand 2-3 ticks; the left hand flutters 3-6 cm. Nothing on the arms locks.

Overlap and follow-through everywhere: the hips lead, the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more, and the sword hand trails its forearm 2-4 ticks so the blade settles after the body (Clip.overlap()). Holds are moving holds, never a repeated pose. Cartoony and readable, not mocap. The coat chains are in the pack, but a spring drives them in the game: leave them at rest, and give the hips and spine real motion for the springs to follow. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees). The blade never passes through the head, the hat, the body or the legs, and it is never pointed straight at the match camera behind him: it always keeps a clear sideways part so its length reads.

fixed: it loops at full speed; the game scales its playback by speed / 10.6 m/s with a 0.35x floor (walk 0.4x, start 0.6x)
the jump starts from any tick of it with a 0.05 s crossfade
adjustable: the cycle length (32 ticks proposed, today's; 0.21 s was too frantic in September)
